summary: The candidate fixes a real pre-normalization GenerateReqInput cleanup AttributeError in create_abort_task, but that function is not the public /abort_request path described by the issue. The endpoint remains unchanged and returns HTTP 200 after local dispatch without downstream completion acknowledgement. Identical real-GPU probes aborted cleanly on base and candidate, so the original endpoint failure was not reproduced and the candidate is only a partial fix.

tests.what_was_measured: Candidate regression failed before the change: three cases raised AttributeError for missing is_single; one normalized batch case passed.
All four candidate cleanup cases passed, confirming the narrow create_abort_task correction.

tests.command: qualified PR649 subreaper runner and HTTP abort probe against recorded base
tests.what_was_measured: HTTP 200 was returned and the active stream ended with finish_reason.type=abort after four tokens; no missing-is_single exception was logged.

tests.command: qualified PR649 subreaper runner and HTTP abort probe against exact candidate
tests.what_was_measured: HTTP 200 was returned and the active stream ended with finish_reason.type=abort after four tokens; no missing-is_single exception was logged.
Only create_abort_task changed; the public /abort_request handler did not change and still directly dispatches then returns 200.

gpu_execution.evidence: Base and candidate performed real generation on one AMD Instinct MI350X/gfx950 with Torch 2.11.0+rocm7.2. The deterministic fixture weight SHA-256 was 6632fab7c351a0bd85518d80a89ec673f68139587f5ad3fa8d5ab38fad87e75f.

remaining_counterexamples: The public /abort_request endpoint is unchanged and does not invoke the modified create_abort_task path.
HTTP 200 still acknowledges only successful local dispatch; there is no scheduler completion acknowledgement or later cancellation-failure propagation.
The original endpoint failure was not reproduced: matched live GPU probes aborted cleanly on both recorded base and exact candidate.
remaining_limitations: The original meta-llama/Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct weights were unavailable.
The report used RTX 4090/CUDA; review execution used one AMD MI350X/gfx950 with ROCm 7.2.
The tiny random Llama fixture validates transport and engine execution only, not semantic accuracy, the original model configuration, NVIDIA behavior, or distributed behavior.
Because the original failure did not reproduce and the endpoint has no completion protocol, no speculative endpoint change was evaluated.
Both owned server process groups exceeded the graceful shutdown window and were killed and reaped.
No native source changed, so a native rebuild was not applicable.
